clauses.current_legal_basis: The provision continues because no end is stated and no instrument ending EO 11552 was found in the searches checked through 2026-10-14: Section 3(a) delegation, as amended by Executive Order 12107 to name the Office of Personnel Management.

later_events.mechanism: amendment (section 2-101 substitutes Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission; effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404)

clauses.reason: Section 3(a) delegates to the United States Civil Service Commission the authority vested in the President by sections 3582(b) and 3584 of title 5, United States Code, except as otherwise provided in the order. Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055, January 3, 1979; signed December 28, 1978) section 2-101 amends each order listed in its section, which includes Executive Order 11552, by substituting Office of Personnel Management for Civil Service Commission, and its section 2-404 makes the order effective January 1, 1979. This is a substitution of the delegate, so under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends; the parent has not been revoked, so Section 3(a) is operative on 2026-10-14 with the Office of Personnel Management as delegate.

clauses.mechanism: performed on issuance (own terms: the revocation took effect when the order was signed)
clauses.reason: Section 4 states that Executive Order No. 10804 of February 12, 1959 'is hereby revoked'. The revocation was performed when the order was issued, so the command is spent from the order's own date, August 24, 1970 (the register date; the held Federal Register text shows the filing date as August 24, 1970 although the OCR drops the day of the signing line). Its effect, the revocation of Executive Order 10804, survives as a consequence and is not a continuing command. This is performance by the order's own terms, not an end imposed by a later instrument.

research_rationale:
Read the held Federal Register text of EO 11552 (35 FR 13569, 3 CFR 1966-1970 Comp. p. 954; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11552.txt) in full. It directs the Secretary of State to lead and coordinate Federal participation in international organizations by details and transfers (Section 1), directs agencies to cooperate by four stated policies (Section 2), delegates authorities under 5 U.S.C. 3343, 3581, 3582(b) and 3584 to the Civil Service Commission and the Secretary of State (Section 3) and revokes Executive Order 10804 (Section 4). The prepared inventory has no clause for Section 3(a) and labels Section 3(b) as Section 2, so it is corrected to twelve clauses by characters. The one held later instrument is Executive Order 12107 (44 FR 1055), whose section 2-101 substitutes the Office of Personnel Management for the Civil Service Commission in this order along with many others, effective January 1, 1979 under section 2-404; it affects only Section 3(a). The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes). Their hits are leads that the order is printed as an amended note to 5 U.S.C. 3584 and cited in the 5 CFR part 352 authority line; the disposition-note search shows only the Executive Order 12107 amendment and no revocation. Eleven clauses are therefore operative on 2026-10-14 (Section 3(a) as amended) under the held original plus bounded search route, and Section 4 is spent by performance on issuance. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the text is the OCR layer of the official page and the day of the signing line is illegible there.
